correctness.rationale: A canonical greedy embedding of the proper prefix of each MAS determines a subset of source one-indices; removing a zero in any nonterminal block forces its exact threshold and the final symbol determines the final threshold. Therefore the map (subset,terminal bit) is injective, giving the binomial upper bound. On (010)^k, an explicit zero-gap formula realizes every pair and single-letter deletion of each resulting word re-embeds by a one-index shift or a threshold adjustment. Direct enumeration of all 4094 binary words of lengths 1..11 and each constructed witness for k=1..9 agrees. The all-k result depends on the proof, not finite tests.

value.rationale: The size of the antichain of minimal forbidden scattered subsequences is a natural combinatorial parameter of the downward-closed subsequence language. A source with k instances of a rare letter can have arbitrarily many copies of the other letter, making input-length bounds poorly informative. The full binomial spectrum and source-length-independent sharp bound give a complete composition-sensitive extremal answer for the binary alphabet. The explicit family (010)^k simultaneously saturates all layers and provides structured witnesses, rather than an arbitrary finite census or a tiny numerical gain.
